about: Feature groups for image_projection.py: each object of a device map belongs to the first group whose pattern (a Python regex over the object name with the build folder stripped, as image_projection.object_name prints it) matches it; the rest are 'other'. 'returns' says whether the group comes back when engine 2 reaches feature parity with the released engine (yes, partly, no); the projection adds the engine-1 bytes of the yes and partly groups. The groups and their answers are those of the 24 Nov 2026 measurement (program analysis ram-flash.md, section 1.4). A parity lane that brings a feature back names its group in its brief and its PR; a lane that moves an object between groups edits this file in the same change.

groups.name: provider loops (openai, mistral, custom, shared loop)
groups.why: Engine 2 speaks to these providers through new wires and one router (ruling 120), not through engine 1's loops: the bytes are an upper bound for what the router adds.

groups.name: anthropic engine-1 loop extras
groups.why: Managed-agent sub-agents and the hosted MCP path inside engine 1's Anthropic loop: back only if those connectors are wanted.

groups.name: images, vision, image generation, provider files
groups.why: Photos as native media and image tools are owner features (rulings on vision).

groups.name: sub-agents and jobs
groups.why: jobs.cpp and the sub-agent provenance; engine 2's plain_agents.cpp is a stub.

groups.name: MCP client, connectors, OAuth
groups.why: Connectors the owner configured on engine 1.

groups.name: memory tools, vector memory, web search
groups.why: Engine 2's notes and search replace part of it.

groups.name: skills
groups.why: Store, attach, built-ins, commands and the web page; skills_device.cpp is already in engine 2.

groups.name: owner tools (models, prefs, device log, open questions, self wakeups)
groups.why: Tools the owner uses on engine 1.

groups.name: dream
groups.why: Probably back, in engine 2's own form.

groups.name: engine-1 file tools
groups.why: Engine 2 has its own file tools (orch_file_tools.cpp).

groups.name: engine-1 prompt machinery
groups.why: The old engine itself: engine 2 replaces it.

groups.name: engine-1 turn machinery in shared objects
groups.why: The old turn's code inside files both engines link; the linker drops it from engine 2.

groups.name: merged strings without an owner
groups.why: The linker lists the merged string blob of the objects linked before it on the first object that contributes (Adafruit NeoPixel esp.c.o on these images); its engine-1 surplus is the strings of the groups above, so the projection adds it in proportion: the share of the other missing bytes that return.
